title: Platform systems & services — team wiki, how‑tos, dashboards, alerts, and runbooks (Q2 2026 addendum)
author: Asha Patel
body:
Overview:

This page is the canonical team‑wiki entry for Platform Systems & Services covering: operational how‑tos, canonical dashboards, alert thresholds, runbooks for common failure modes, retrospective action items, and the near‑term roadmap (Q2 2026 addendum). Use this page as the first stop for onboarding new SREs and platform engineers, and for runbook escalation during incidents.

Owners and contacts:
- Team: Platform Systems & Services (eng‑platform)
- Primary oncall rotation: platform‑sre (PagerDuty)
- Slack channel: #platform‑ops
- Doc owner: Asha Patel (eng‑platform)
- Secondary contacts: Liam O'Connor (Observability), Priya Singh (Runtime), Daniel Morales (Infra)

Quick links (single line):
- Playbook: /confluence/eng-platform/platform-systems-and-services-playbook-2026.json
- Capacity runbooks: /confluence/eng-platform/platform-systems-services-capacity-planning-2025.json
- Incident postmortems: /confluence/oncall-and-incident-response/postmortems/

1) Systems & services inventory (high level)
- platform-controller: Kubernetes control plane helpers / job routing / rollout orchestration. Owner: eng‑platform (Priya). SLO: 99.95% availability, p99 API latency < 450ms.
- observability-service: Ingest + storage for metrics and traces (Prometheus remote_write -> Cortex; Jaeger tracing). Owner: Observability subteam (Liam). Retention: metrics 90d, traces 30d.
- platform-cache: Redis cluster used for prefix/KV caching for inference routing. Owner: Runtime (Daniel). SLA: 99.9%, failover via multi‑AZ.
- model-router: Smart routing service that selects model variant and region. Owner: Runtime. Important config: max_concurrent_shards=64, default_routing_policy=latency

2) Canonical dashboards (what to look at)
- platform-health (Grafana): cluster CPU/memory, pod restart rate, node pressure, kube api latencies.
- runtime-throughput (Grafana): requests/s, tokens/s, batch size distribution, p50/p95/p99 latency per model.
- cost-visibility (Grafana): GPU utilization by pool, idle GPU hours, batching efficiency.
- alerts-overview (Grafana): active alerts by severity and owner.

Dashboard notes / panels to add: 1) batch size histograms (last 24h), 2) KV cache hit rate, 3) model-variant fallback count.

3) Alerting thresholds & rationale (Prometheus/Alertmanager)
- platform_controller_high_api_latency: trigger when kube_api_latency_p95 > 450ms for 2m. Priority: P1. Owner: eng‑platform. Runbook: Platform controller slow API runbook (below).
- runtime_high_error_rate: trigger when request_http_error_rate > 0.5% (5m) for model_router. Priority: P1. Action: route to fallback model variant or increase capacity.
- gpu_pool_memory_pressure: trigger when GPU_mem_used / GPU_mem_total > 0.88 for 5m. Priority: P2. Action: scale capacity or drain low‑priority jobs.
- cache_degradation: trigger when platform_cache_kv_hit_rate < 70% for 10m. Priority: P2. Action: investigate eviction/tuning, warm critical prefixes.
- prometheus_rule_firing_count > 30 (10m): meta‑alert to indicate multiple correlated failures. Priority: P0.

Alerting principles:
- Alerts must map to a runbook with a clear owner.
- Avoid flappy thresholds: require >=2 evaluation windows where applicable.
- All P1/P0 alerts page the rotation and create a Slack thread in #platform‑ops.

4) Runbooks (step‑by‑step)
A) Platform controller — slow API (p95 > 450ms)
1. Confirm alert: check grafana panel platform_controller -> api latency p95 and API server logs (kubectl logs).
2. Check api server pod restarts: kubectl get pods -n kube-system -l component=kube-apiserver.
3. Inspect etcd health: etcdctl --endpoints=$ETCD_ENDPOINT endpoint status. If etcd latency high, escalate to Storage owner.
4. If high CPU on control plane nodes: scale control plane (follow runbook: /confluence/eng-platform/control-plane-scale-2025).
5. If cause is increased request rate from model-router: temporarily enable rate limiting rule for non‑critical routes (config: rate_limits.yaml).
6. If unresolved after 30 minutes, open an incident and include: replay of p99 traces, node/etcd metrics, recent deploys.

B) Runtime — elevated error rate for model serving
1. Identify affected model(s) and variants in request logs (trace id examples).
2. Check batch size distribution: if median batch size < configured min_batch_size, routing mis‑batching may cause errors.
3. Route degraded traffic to fallback_variant (config key: fallback_policy.default_variant).
4. If errors persist, scale model pool (increase replicas or move to dedicated GPU pool).
5. Capture sample inputs and add to regression suite for triage.

C) GPU memory pressure
1. Validate alert: check gpu_pool_exporter.memory_usage and node free memory.
2. Drain non‑critical/low‑priority pods: kubectl drain --selector=priority=low --ignore-daemons.
3. If sustained > 20m, trigger capacity increase (auto or manual) and notify capacity team.

Runbook best practices:
- Each runbook contains: purpose, owner, symptoms, diagnostic commands, mitigation steps, escalation contacts, post‑incident actions.
- Keep runbooks under 10 steps for common incidents; link deeper diagnostics if needed.

5) Retrospective summary (last 3 incidents, Q4 2025 — Q1 2026)
- Incident: Model-router latency spike (2025-12-07)
  - Root cause: unbounded request storm from one customer causing small batch sizes and CPU saturation.
  - Actions: implement per‑customer ingress rate limits; add batching metrics to alerts; add automated fallback to compatible model variants.
  - Status: rate limits rolled out (2026-01-15), monitoring added.
- Incident: Observability ingest backlog (2026-01-23)
  - Root cause: retention compaction job misconfiguration caused headblock growth in Cortex.
  - Actions: fixed compaction config, added compaction health alert (prometheus_rule).
  - Status: completed and verified.
- Incident: Redis eviction storms on platform_cache (2026-02-02)
  - Root cause: sudden workload shift causing cache miss amplification.
  - Actions: increase maxmemory, tuned eviction policy, pre‑warm critical prefixes in traffic.
  - Status: mitigations in place; permanent fix tracked on roadmap.

6) Roadmap (Q2 2026 addendum — priorities and owners)
- Q2 2026 (May–Jun): Capacity & autoscaling improvements
  - Deliverable: predictive autoscaler for GPU pools (owner: Daniel) — ETA: 2026-06-20.
  - Deliverable: autoscaler metrics dashboard + runbook — ETA: 2026-06-30.
- Q3 2026 (planning): Observability scaling
  - Deliverable: move Prometheus long‑term storage to Cortex federated clusters (owner: Liam) — planning in Q2.
- Ongoing: Runbook hygiene & exercise program
  - Deliverable: quarterly game‑days to validate runbooks (owner: Asha) — first run scheduled 2026-05-12.

7) How‑tos / quick procedures (for common operational tasks)
- Oncall runbook update flow (2 step): 1) If you change an alert threshold, update runbook and reviewers then 2) add a short note to #platform‑ops + PR to docs repo.
- Adding a dashboard panel: fork grafana‑dashboards repo -> add panel JSON -> create PR with screenshots and panel description -> reviewers: Observability + two platform engineers.
- Emergency capacity increase: follow capacity runbook, include change request number, and notify Sales and Product for potential customer impact.

8) Team wiki housekeeping rules
- Keep pages short and link to deeper docs.
- Add an owner and last_updated date on each child page.
- Tag runbooks with labels: runbook, severity (P0|P1|P2), owner_team.
- Monthly doc audit: owners must confirm content accuracy or mark archive.

Appendix: Config snippets and commands (examples)
- Check model routing p95 latency (promql):
  sum(rate(model_router_request_duration_seconds_bucket[5m])) by (le)
- Warm cache prefix example (curl):
  curl -X POST -H 'Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN' https://cache-internal.redwood/api/v1/warm -d '{"prefix":"/customer/12345"}'
- Sample kubectl for draining low priority nodes: kubectl drain node-21 --ignore-daemonsets --force --delete-local-data 

Post‑incident actions (must include in every P1/P0 incident):
1) Assign action owner within 48h.
2) Create a ticket with tracked remediation and ETA.
3) Add regression test to eval harness if applicable.
4) Verify fix in next game‑day.

If you find missing runbooks, annotate this page and assign to the runbook backlog (label: runbook‑todo).
